title: Governmental Accounting - GASB Standards
learning_objectives: Account for capital assets and long-term debt

overview.key_difference: Fund accounting - separate accounting entities for different purposes
overview.financial_reporting: Dual perspective: Government-wide (accrual) and Fund (mostly modified accrual)

governmental_funds.operating_statement_name: Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances

proprietary_funds.operating_statement_name: Statement of Revenues, Expenses, and Changes in Net Position

modified_accrual.available: Collectible within current period or soon enough to pay current liabilities (typically within 60 days)
key_differences_from_full_accrual: Capital asset purchases = Expenditures (not capitalized in fund statements)
Interest on long-term debt = Expenditure when due (not accrued)
Depreciation NOT recorded in governmental funds

general_fund.examples: General government operations, police, fire, administration

special_revenue.purpose: Specific revenue sources restricted for specific purposes
special_revenue.examples: Gas tax fund, grants, hotel tax for tourism

debt_service.purpose: Accumulate resources for debt principal and interest payments

permanent_funds.purpose: Earnings (not principal) used for government programs

enterprise_funds.purpose: Business-type activities (fees charged to external users)

internal_service.purpose: Services provided to other government departments

statements.name: Statement of Activities
statements.format: By function (public safety, education, etc.) with revenues netted against expenses

hierarchy_most_to_least_restricted.description: Cannot be spent (inventory, prepaid, permanent fund principal)
Self-imposed by highest level of government (council resolution)
Intended for specific purpose (less formal than committed)
Residual (only in General Fund, can be negative in others)

fund_balance_classifications.spending_order: Restricted first, then Committed, then Assigned, then Unassigned (unless policy specifies otherwise)

property_taxes.recognition: When levied and available (adjusted for uncollectible)
property_taxes.modified_accrual:
DR Property Tax Receivable
DR Allowance for Uncollectible
   CR Property Tax Revenue
   CR Deferred Inflows (amounts not available)

sales_taxes.recognition: When underlying transaction occurs if measurable and available
sales_taxes.note: Often collected by state and remitted to locality

capital_assets.governmental_funds: Capital outlays recorded as Expenditures (not capitalized in fund statements)
capital_assets.government_wide: Capitalized and depreciated (except infrastructure if using modified approach)
capital_assets.infrastructure: Roads, bridges, etc. - capitalize and depreciate (or use modified approach with condition assessment)

governmental_funds.balance: NOT reported in fund balance sheet

cpa_exam_strategies.fund_identification: Governmental (modified accrual, current resources) vs. Proprietary (full accrual, economic resources) vs. Fiduciary (hold for others).
cpa_exam_strategies.modified_accrual: Revenue: Available + Measurable. Expenditure: When incurred. Capital purchases = Expenditures. No depreciation.
cpa_exam_strategies.fund_balance: Remember hierarchy: N-R-C-A-U (Nonspendable, Restricted, Committed, Assigned, Unassigned).
cpa_exam_strategies.government_wide: Full accrual, capitalizes assets, reports long-term debt. Reconcile to fund statements.
cpa_exam_strategies.common_tested: Modified accrual revenue recognition, fund balance classifications, reconciliation between fund and government-wide statements.

key_points: Governmental funds: Modified accrual, current resources focus
Proprietary funds: Full accrual, economic resources (like commercial)
Fiduciary funds: Hold resources for others, not in government-wide statements
Modified accrual: Revenue when available + measurable. Capital purchases = Expenditures.
Government-wide: Full accrual, reports capital assets and long-term debt
General Fund always major fund, always reported separately
